key_findings: SNI induces mechanical allodynia and sleep disruption comorbidity, with hyperactivity of dorsal lateral septum GABAergic neurons.
Chemogenetic/optogenetic inhibition of LSD GABAergic neurons relieves allodynia and sleep disruption; activation induces both in naive mice.
Dexmedetomidine (25 ug/kg i.p. or intra-LSD) reduces LSD GABAergic hyperactivity via α2A adrenergic receptors, relieving pain and sleep disruption; blocked by yohimbine or α2A knockdown.
LS GABA to LPO glutamatergic and LPO GABAergic circuits mediate allodynia and sleep disruption, respectively.
